annotations.text:
Liquid Glass — iOS 26

All three use the same material: blurred, saturated, translucent panels with a specular top edge, floating over a coloured bed. They differ only in how loud that bed is. Real menu data from Monday 1 September.

A — Topla glazura

Warm amber/plum/teal bed, saturated. The glass has plenty to refract, so it reads unmistakably as iOS 26.

Tradeoff: the most decorative of the three. On a screen you open twice a week that is fine; if you find it busy after a fortnight, C is the same design turned down.

B — Svetla glazura

Same material inverted. Light glass is what iOS actually shows most of the day, and food reads better on a bright ground.

Tradeoff: no dark mode here yet, and this is a phone you'll often check in a dim corridor. It would need a dark variant built alongside, so it is the most work.

C — Mirna glazura

Identical structure, near-monochrome bed and a sand accent instead of amber. The glass reads as depth rather than as colour.

Tradeoff: closest to what you have now, so it is the smallest jump — but it is also the least distinctive, and it fixes 'brutal' more than it earns 'nice'.
